subject: Throughput runway, benchmark plan and economics — MAP & close timeline
messages:
From: Tyler Brooks <tyler@finova.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finova.com
Date: 2027-10-10T15:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro — MAP request: throughput & econ targets

Hi Lukas,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Procurement would like a short mutual action plan we can circulate internally outlining the performance acceptance criteria (latency, sustained QPS/TTFT, concurrency), the evaluation plan (test harness, datasets, scoring), and a target close timeline.

High level targets from our side:
- Sustained QPS: 450 requests/sec (average 1.2k tokens/request)
- Peak concurrency: 1200 concurrent requests
- TTFT target: <= 65ms at P50, <= 120ms at P95
- Cost target: ideally <$0.004 per 1k tokens served (including caching)

Can you sketch a MAP and let us know what artifacts (datasets, runbooks, access) you need to run a representative sustained throughput test? We need this internally by EOW.

—Tyler
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
To: Tyler Brooks <tyler@finova.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-11T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Re: Intro — MAP request: throughput & econ targets

Tyler — thanks, good targets and very clear. Attached is a one-page MAP & evaluation checklist that lines up milestones with dates. Quick summary of what we propose:

1) MAP milestones (target close: 2027-10-28)
  - Day 0 (today): Share canonical prompt set + sample traffic profile (you)
  - Day 2: Redwood runs small-scale dry-run (smoke) on hosted cluster
  - Day 5: Sustained throughput run (48h) on dedicated capacity; produce token/sec, sustained QPS, TTFT distributions
  - Day 7: Joint readout and economics modeling; close decision window

2) Evaluation plan (what we run)
  - Test harness: included (k6 wrapper + internal runner) with ability to replay tokenized traffic and maintain KV cache warmups
  - Metrics captured: tokens/sec, sustained QPS (1m/5m windows), TTFT (P50/P90/P95), tail latency (P99), GPU utilization, memory/KV cache hit rate
  - Pass criteria: sustain >= 420 QPS for 24h with P95 TTFT <= 140ms; optional canary at 450 QPS

3) Unit economics deliverables
  - Per-run token accounting + compute hours, cost model with batching and caching assumptions
  - Expected unit cost range: $0.0038–$0.006/token-per-1k depending on batching and quantization profile (we'll provide model variants)

Attachments: finova_map_v1.xlsx (MAP & milestones), test_harness_instructions.md (link in Drive).

We need: your canonical prompt set, expected tokens/request distribution, and a HubSpot PO or approval to schedule Dedicated cluster time.

I'll have Neha run the first smoke test tomorrow and circulate results.

Cheers,
Lukas

--
Lukas Meyer
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tyler Brooks <tyler@finova.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-13T14:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Throughput runway, benchmark plan and economics — MAP & close timeline

Hi Tyler — per the MAP we kicked off the smoke runs today. Notes from the run and attached raw results (throughput_results_10-17.csv):

Smoke summary (hosted cluster, synthetic replay of 1k requests, 1.2k tokens/request avg):
- Peak tokens/sec: 980k tokens/sec (burst)
- Sustained tokens/sec (10m windows): 410–460k tokens/sec depending on KV cache warm state
- Sustained QPS observed: 340–460 QPS (mean 405 QPS) over 2-hour window
- TTFT: P50 58ms, P95 118ms, P99 210ms (note: P99 improved when we increased batching window)
- Concurrency during peak: ~980 concurrent flows
- GPU utilization: 78–92% across the run (autoscaler headroom ~12%)

Unit economics (initial model attached in unit_econ_summary.pdf):
- Measured tokens in run: 3.6B tokens over 2 hours (simulated traffic)
- Effective per-1k-token compute cost (run-based, not including infra overhead): $0.0032 with standard batching; $0.0026 if we enable PQ8 quantization profile and tighter batching (tradeoff: slight latency delta at P99)
- Estimated total per-1k-token delivered (including network and storage amortization): $0.0038–$0.0045

Observations and suggested next steps:
1) To hit your 450 QPS sustained target we recommend a dedicated 48h run with warmed KV cache and request shaping to reflect your real-world distribution (we saw warm vs cold makes ~12% difference).
2) We can run a canary at 450 QPS for 6h to validate tail latency before the 48h window.
3) If procurement signs off by Monday (10/18) we can provision dedicated capacity and run the 48h by 10/21 and have a joint readout on 10/24.

Attaching the CSV and the unit economics PDF. Let me know any adjustments to the test profile.

-Neha
From: Tyler Brooks <tyler@finova.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finova.com
Date: 2027-10-14T10:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Throughput runway, benchmark plan and economics — MAP & close timeline

Thanks Neha — this is very helpful and gives us confidence. A couple of quick clarifications:
1) When you say "tokens/sec" are you reporting tokenized model tokens (BPE) or input characters? We want to ensure our on-prem request shaping produces the same token distribution.
2) The unit economics number looks compelling; can you provide a variant that includes a 20% enterprise support uplift and 12-month retention costs? Procurement asked for both scenarios.

Procurement is targeting internal approval on 10/18; if that lands we will accept the 10/21–10/24 test window. Please include an explicit canary step and an acceptance gate (sign-off: Finova SRE + Redwood SE) in the MAP. Also please send a DocuSign with the reserved capacity quote once you have the final numbers.

—Tyler
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Tyler Brooks <tyler@finova.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-18T18:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Throughput runway, benchmark plan and economics — MAP & close timeline

Tyler — quick replies inline: 
1) tokens/sec = BPE tokens as measured by our tokenizer; we'll include your tokenizer in the replay to ensure parity.
2) Attached is an updated unit_econ_summary.pdf that includes 
   - Scenario A: base pricing (no uplift) — $0.0038 per 1k tokens (delivery)
   - Scenario B: +20% enterprise support uplift — $0.00456 per 1k tokens
   - Scenario C: +12% retention & audit overhead amortized — $0.00499 per 1k tokens

We've added a formal canary gate in the MAP workbook and a DocuSign link (https://docs.example/ds/FIN-2027-0917) for the reserved capacity quote. If procurement signs off today we'll schedule the canary on 10/21 02:00–08:00 UTC and the 48h sustained run 10/21–10/23. Joint readout 10/24 at 16:00 UTC.

Action items:
- Finova: provide canonical prompt set + tokenizer + traffic profile (ASAP)
- Procurement: finalize PO/DocuSign by 10/18 EOD
- Redwood: reserve dedicated cluster and share runbook (Neha)

I'll follow up with the DocuSign and updated MAP workbook.

Thanks,
Rishi

Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
